Build a plugin dataset (administrators)

Administrators build the datasets plugins need — a join, a filter, a total — with the no-SQL query builder in Administrator → Database → Plugin datasets, preview what a plugin would read, and publish them to every plugin editor and SATOM Builder.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage studio.plugin_studio
📍 WhereAdministrator → System → Database → Plugin datasets (URLs /database/#tab-plugin-datasets, /database/plugin-datasets/new)

What is it?#

A plugin dataset is a read-only query an administrator builds for plugins to read, next to SATOM's built-in datasets and the device-object ones. You build it without SQL — the same four-step query builder as the database reports — preview the rows a plugin would get, and publish it. From then on every Report Studio editor, the Python console and SATOM Builder offer it as admin_<name>.

What does it do?#

  • Build a query: a base table, related tables (joined on their keys, including inferred ones), columns, filters with value suggestions, grouping with totals, order and a row limit (at most 500).
  • Preview what a plugin reads for your ADOM: the first rows and the column names the plugin uses.
  • Draft or publish. A draft is visible only here; a published dataset is offered to plugins of its ADOM (or of every ADOM).
  • Unpublish without deleting; delete only when no plugin reads it.
  • Approve a dataset that came in with an imported package (pending approval).
  • See who uses it: the list names the plugins that read each dataset.

Requirements#

  • The tables you need exist in the Report Builder catalogue (the Relational model tab shows them). Credential tables and sensitive columns are never offered.
  • The database's read-only role is usable (the SQL console works).

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the Database page and the Plugin datasets tab users.manage
Create, edit, preview, publish, unpublish, approve, delete users.manage and studio.plugin_studio
Read a published dataset in a plugin Whoever opens the plugin; rows are cut to their ADOM and devices

Without studio.plugin_studio the tab lists the datasets but offers no New plugin dataset and no row actions; the pages answer 403. A profile confined to some ADOMs cannot open the Database page at all.

How to use#

Build and publish a dataset#

  1. Go to Administrator → System → Database and open the Plugin datasets tab. The banner counts the datasets plugins can already read (built-in, published here, device objects per product).
  2. Click New plugin dataset.
  3. Fill in Key (after the fixed admin_: a letter, then lowercase letters, digits and _), Name, ADOM (Every ADOM or one product) and Description — what an author reads in the picker.
  4. Click Build the query (no SQL) and walk the four steps:
  5. Base table — for example Server Policies (device cache).
  6. Related tables — tick Appliances (fleet) to get the device name.
  7. Columns & filters — tick the columns; add filters.
  8. Group, order & limit — choose an aggregate per column to total, the order and the row limit. Click Generate SQL. The page shows the SQL it compiles to (read-only) and runs a Preview.
  9. Read the preview line: N row(s) for your ADOM; a plugin reads the columns …. These column names are what a view writes: {{ r.vserver }}.
  10. Choose Status → Published and click Save.

The dataset is now in every plugin picker of its ADOM, under Administrator datasets, and in SATOM Builder at its next library refresh.

Change a dataset#

Open it with the pencil. Build the query starts the builder from scratch; to change one filter, edit Query as JSON (base, joins, columns, filters, group_by, order_by, limit) and click Preview, then Save. The Key never changes: plugins name the dataset by it. A change applies to the plugins that read it at their next render.

Approve a dataset an import brought#

When a view is imported from another SATOM with an administrator dataset this server does not have, the import creates that dataset pending approval and the tab shows a count on its title. Open it: the banner names the package it came with. Check the query and the preview, choose Published and Save — or use the Approve and publish button in the list. Until then, the view renders with no rows from it.

Unpublish or delete#

  • Unpublish (eye-slash) hides it from pickers; plugins that read it get no rows from it — the message names them.
  • Delete is refused while any plugin reads it: remove it from those plugins first (or unpublish it).

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Key admin_ + a letter and up to 59 lowercase letters, digits, _; unique; never changes Yes admin_policy_inventory
Name Shown in pickers and the Library Yes Server policy inventory
ADOM Every ADOM or one product: the ADOMs whose plugins are offered it No Every ADOM
Status Draft or Published Yes Published
Description What an author reads No Every cached server policy with its device
Query Report Builder query: base, joins (at most 4), columns, filters (at most 10), group_by, order_by, limit (at most 500) Yes —

Column names a plugin reads. A plain column keeps its own name; when two tables in the query have a column with the same name, both read <table>_<column> (appliances_name, device_server_policies_name). An aggregate reads n (count), count_distinct_<col>, sum_<col>, avg_<col>, min_<col>, max_<col>.

Example#

🧪Example — Server policies with the name of their device

Base device_server_policies; join appliances (on appliance_id → id) and device_objects (on object_id → id); columns appliances.name, appliance_id, name, vserver, server_pool, web_protection_profile, status; filter device_objects.layer = config (the cache keeps one row per layer — without it every policy shows twice); order by name; limit 500.

Key admin_policy_inventory. A view reads:

{% for r in admin_policy_inventory.rows %}
  {{ r.appliances_name }} — {{ r.device_server_policies_name }} ({{ r.status }})
{% endfor %}

Result#

  • The dataset is stored in SATOM's database (table plugin_datasets) and replicated with it.
  • Every create, update, status change and delete writes an audit line (plugin_dataset.create, plugin_dataset.update, plugin_dataset.status, plugin_dataset.delete; an import writes plugin_dataset.pending).
  • A view that exports with it carries its definition in the package.

Troubleshooting#

"Key: a letter, then lowercase letters, digits and _ (2 to 60)."#

Possible causes - Upper-case letters, a dash, a space, or a key starting with a digit.

Solution 1. Use policy_inventory, not Policy-Inventory.

"admin_… already exists."#

Possible causes - Another dataset (perhaps pending, from an import) has that key.

Solution 1. Open the existing one, or choose another key.

"The key cannot change: plugins name the dataset by it. Create a new one."#

Solution 1. Create a new dataset with the new key, move the plugins to it, then delete the old one.

"column '….…' is sensitive and cannot be used"#

Possible causes - The column holds a credential or looks like one (password, secret, token…).

Solution 1. Leave it out. Plugins never read credentials.

"… belongs to no ADOM, and your profile is confined to some ADOMs: it cannot read that table"#

Possible causes - A table without a product, device or kind column, previewed by a profile confined to some ADOMs.

Solution 1. Build the dataset with an unconfined administrator, or use tables that belong to an ADOM.

The preview shows every row twice#

Possible causes - The query reads a cache projection (device_server_policies, device_server_pools, device_web_protection_profiles), which keeps one row per cache layer.

Solution 1. Join device_objects on object_id → id and filter device_objects.layer = config.

Verification - The preview's row count equals the number of objects.

"… cannot be published: …"#

Possible causes - The query no longer compiles on this server (a pending dataset from another SATOM version, a table that changed).

Solution 1. Open it, rebuild or fix the query, Preview, then publish.

"… is read by …: remove it from those plugins first (or unpublish it)."#

Solution 1. Edit each named plugin and untick the dataset, then delete it.

Advanced How it works
  • The registry is services.plugin_datasets: built-in datasets come from plugin_sandbox.DATASETS, device-object ones from the device cache (device_objects, re-scanned at most every five minutes per worker), administrator ones from the plugin_datasets table.
  • An administrator dataset compiles through the Report Builder (catalogue-checked identifiers, sensitive columns refused, SELECT only) and runs through db_lookup as the read-only console role, with the ADOM scope of the viewer added to every table (a product column, an appliance_id, or an appliance's kind), then cut to the viewer's visible devices.
  • SATOM Builder receives the definition (spec) in GET /api/v1/builder/library and the rows in GET /api/v1/builder/data, with the token owner's scope.
